title: Study to assess the effectiveness and safety of a treatment using light and a special cream (Ameluz®) in people with weakened immune systems who have skin lesions caused by the sun or a mild type of skin cancer, anywhere on the body.
official: Evaluation of the efficacy and safety of photodynamic therapy with BF-200 ALA (Ameluz®) in immunosuppressed patients with actinic keratoses and superficial basal cell carcinoma at any location.
summary: Main objective: Evaluate the efficacy and safety of photodynamic therapy (PDT) with BF-200 ALA in immunosuppressed patients compared to non-immunosuppressed patients with grade I–II actinic keratosis and superficial basal cell carcinoma.
conditions: Immunosuppressed patients with premalignant and malignant skin lesions, such as actinic keratosis (AK), cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), and basal cell carcinoma (BCC), due to chronic immunosuppression.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. Immunosuppressed patients (transplant recipients and those with hematological diseases, specifically chronic lymphocytic leukemia and multiple myeloma)
3. Clinical and histological diagnosis of grade I/II actinic keratoses (3 to 9 AKs) and/or basal cell carcinomas (1 to 3 BCCs, 0.5 to 2 cm in diameter, located on the face/scalp, neck, trunk, or extremities)
4. Ability to provide informed consent
5. Availability for follow-up at 3, 6, and 12 months
Exclusion criteria:
1. Known allergy to 5-ALA, peanuts, soy, or any component of BF-200 ALA
2. Porphyria or other photosensitive disorders
3. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
4. Use of topical treatments in the treatment area within the previous 12 weeks or during the study
5. Prior treatment in the target area with more than 5 therapies before the study, to avoid treatment-resistant actinic keratoses
6. Participation in a clinical trial within the last 30 days
7. Treatment with substances  with phototoxic or photoallergic potential within the previous 8 weeks
